CHAPTER 1
A reader contract for this edition
Paper XI develops packet decomposition, finite representation comparisons, actual arithmetic/type adapters, and
a conditional comparison interface. This guide makes the logical boundaries visible in the source language. The
traditional paper gives the mathematical exposition. The visual guide illustrates the constructions. The retained
Lean sources provide the formal statements and proofs at their printed hypotheses.
The general arithmetic realization endpoint is presented as Conjecture 66. Conjecture 66 isolates the missing
realization claim from historical Claim 16.2, indexed as original obligation 66. This separation preserves the proved
finite comparison and the proved conditional implication. It records that finite assembly and coherent transport
have not yet supplied an actual supercuspidal realization in the original generality.
The accompanying release includes Markdown (.md) files containing detailed proofs, construction notes, proof
audits, and research records. These documents distinguish established results, conditional results, and the re-
maining obligations associated with Conjecture 66.
1.1 What Lean certifies
Acceptance by Lean checks that the declared conclusion follows from its binders, imported declarations, and foun-
dational axioms. It does not silently instantiate a local field, an arithmetic type, a reference correspondence, or a
normalized local-factor convention. Those objects must appear in the source or in a separate mathematical attach-
ment.
A structure may contain an existence field. A theorem that consumes that structure proves an implication using
the field. It is still a substantive theorem when the comparison map, descent or uniqueness is constructed. It is
not a proof of the structure’s arithmetic existence. In particular, Realization.exists_atom is an existence input in
the formal comparison interface.
1.2 Evidence available for this guide
The source catalog was generated for the inherited edition from retained production source bytes. This edition
preserves its selected modules, source hashes, import edges and named lexical records. A separately dated fresh
execution replays the selected source in the pinned environment and audits its actual declaration dependencies.
The current result is summarized below. Historical compiler and same-kernel records later in this guide retain
their original dates and scopes. The preserved catalog’s historical evidence flags describe the edition in which that
catalog was generated; the dated current receipts determine this release’s execution status. The PDF build and the
formal execution are separate operations.
Fresh verification, 18 October 2026: all required gates passed. The 423 selected publication modules
were compiled with their retained source hashes unchanged. All 4,342 catalogued names resolved to
their recorded owners. Four source names—two private theorems and two named local instances—
are matched uniquely to their kernel names using Lean’s own private-name mapping; the source and
kernel names are both recorded. The recovered terminal and the new comparison supplement were
checked as separately counted targets.

system identifies their isomorphism classes if their declared factor profiles agree. The additional module PaperX

CHAPTER 2
Fourier projectors and Frobenius transport
The cyclic packet is constructed by averaging against an additive character. Idempotence, orthogonality and com-
pleteness are consequences of the representation law and character orthogonality. The packet space is the actual
range of the computed projector, and Frobenius transports that range by its conjugation law.
2.0.1 The averaging operator
The ambient cyclic representation and additive-character hypotheses are declared in the source module. The
index is a residue label in Z/MZ. The scalar field is C, so the finite order is invertible. The definition sums actual
operators. Later results compute their products rather than postulating a family of orthogonal idempotents.

Induction, return scalars and tensor
interactions

# Uniformizers of actual matrix-embedded local fields
For a continuous algebra embedding of a local field `E` into matrices over
`F`, its actual uniformizer has nonzero determinant degree over `F`.
The proof uses actual compact integral units and actual uniformizer coordinates;
it does not assume a determinant-norm formula or a ramification index.
Consequently no nonzero power belongs to any compact matrix subgroup.
The embedding may be noncentral. No simple-type realization is asserted here.

SHA-256: c69f0838adb9db017a926ff1a66606634858bfb0aa89710e147b19b44a60d561.
# Compact subgroups have zero integer degree
A continuous integer degree has finite image on a compact subgroup, because
the target has its usual discrete topology.
The image is a finite subgroup of
the torsion-free group `Multiplicative ℤ`, so it is trivial.

# Reduced graph loops and their abelianization
Edges belong to the original quiver. A path in its symmetrification can traverse
an edge in either direction. The free groupoid identifies paths under insertion
and deletion of an edge followed by its reverse. Based endomorphisms therefore
give the combinatorial fundamental group, with multiplication ordered as function
composition: `x * y` traverses `y` before `x`.
`H1` is the abelianization of this actual path quotient. No comparison with a
topological realization or singular homology is asserted here.

The residue--Frobenius pullback retains a decomposition-group coordinate and an
integer degree.
Its degree kernel is inertia.
This file proves the precise
first-isomorphism statement and compares the quotient with the integer-degree
unramified model only under an explicit degree-one Frobenius-lift hypothesis.
It also proves the exact representation-theoretic information loss: a
representation pulled back only through integer degree kills every lower
ramification subgroup, so every ramification depth projector is the identity
and every positive detail projector is zero.
